setting.world: Kansas in the United States and the magical Land of Oz
setting.description: A gray drought-baked Kansas farm prairie with a small one-room house, contrasted with the Land of Oz, a magical country cut off by desert with distinct colored regions, yellow-brick roads, forests, rivers, poppy fields, china villages, and the green-marble Emerald City at its center.

characters.name: Dorothy
characters.physical_description: A well-grown little girl for her age with a merry voice. She typically wears a faded blue-and-white checked gingham dress, a pink sunbonnet.

characters.name: Uncle Henry
characters.physical_description: A stern, solemn farmer gray from his long beard to his rough boots. He is a hard-working older man in farm clothes.

characters.name: Aunt Em
characters.physical_description: A thin and gaunt woman with sober gray eyes and gray cheeks and lips. She wears plain farmwife clothes.

characters.name: Toto
characters.physical_description: A little black dog with long silky hair, small black twinkling eyes, and a funny wee nose. He is small enough to be carried in Dorothy's arms.

characters.name: Scarecrow
characters.physical_description: A stuffed man with a small sack head filled with straw bearing painted eyes, nose, mouth and ears. He wears a pointed old blue Munchkin hat, a worn faded blue suit stuffed with straw, and old boots with blue tops.

characters.name: Tin Woodman
characters.physical_description: A man made entirely of shining jointed tin with head, body, arms and legs joined by hinges. He carries a sharp chopping axe and an oil-can and moves stiffly when rusted.

characters.name: Cowardly Lion
characters.physical_description: A great lion as big as a small horse with a shaggy mane and sharp claws. He is a large, powerful tawny beast with a soft shaggy mane.

characters.name: Oz
characters.physical_description: A little old bald-headed man with a wrinkled face. He dresses in ordinary clothes and hides behind large false forms including a giant paper head, a lady, a beast, and a ball of fire.

characters.name: Wicked Witch of the West
characters.physical_description: An old wicked woman with only one powerful telescope-like eye and skinny limbs. She wears a witch's dress and carries an umbrella and a silver whistle and a Golden Cap.

characters.name: Wicked Witch of the East
characters.physical_description: An old wicked witch seen only as two feet sticking from under a house. She wears silver shoes with pointed toes.

characters.name: Witch of the North
characters.physical_description: A little old wrinkled woman with nearly white hair walking rather stiffly. She wears a white pleated gown sprinkled with diamond-like stars and a white pointed hat with bells.

characters.name: Glinda
characters.physical_description: A beautiful young woman with rich red hair in flowing ringlets over her shoulders and kind blue eyes. She wears a pure white dress and sits on a throne of rubies.

characters.name: Boq
characters.physical_description: A rich Munchkin man about as tall as a well-grown child. He wears a blue round pointed hat with bells, blue clothes, and polished boots with a deep roll of blue at the tops.

characters.name: Guardian of the Gates
characters.physical_description: A little man about Munchkin size clothed all in green with greenish-tinted skin. He carries a large green box of green spectacles and a golden key.

characters.name: Soldier with the green whiskers
characters.physical_description: A soldier dressed in a green uniform with a long green beard and green whiskers. He guards the Palace door.

characters.name: Queen of the Field Mice
characters.physical_description: A tiny little gray field mouse. She is a very small gray mouse with a squeaky voice.

characters.name: King of the Winged Monkeys
characters.physical_description: A much bigger winged monkey than the others with immense powerful wings, long hairy arms and an ugly grinning face. He leads a band of monkeys each with a pair of large wings on the shoulders.

characters.name: Gayelette
characters.physical_description: A beautiful princess and powerful sorceress who lived in the North. She is a beautiful woman in rich robes from a ruby palace.

characters.name: Quelala
characters.physical_description: A handsome, manly young man grown strong and lovely. He wears a rich costume of pink silk and purple velvet.

chapters.title: The Cyclone
chapters.summary: Dorothy lives a gray life on the Kansas prairie with Uncle Henry, Aunt Em, and her black dog Toto. When a cyclone approaches, Uncle Henry runs to the stock and Aunt Em hides in the cyclone cellar, but Dorothy misses her escape while chasing Toto. The house is lifted into the still center of the cyclone and carried miles away as Dorothy rescues Toto and falls asleep on her bed.
chapters.cover_description: A small dull gray Kansas farmhouse whirling high in the dark center of a massive cyclone, lifted like a feather above the flat gray prairie while winds howl around it.

chapters.title: The Council with the Munchkins
chapters.summary: After the cyclone drops her house in the beautiful Munchkin Country, Dorothy is greeted as a sorceress for killing the Wicked Witch of the East with her falling house. The Good Witch of the North explains the four witches of Oz, gives Dorothy the dead witch's charmed silver shoes, and, unable to send her home across the surrounding desert, protects her with a kiss and sends her down the yellow brick road to ask the Great Wizard Oz in the City of Emeralds for help.
chapters.cover_description: Dorothy in her gingham dress standing in the doorway of her little farmhouse dropped in a marvelous Munchkin land of flowers and fruit trees, facing the tiny blue-hatted Munchkins and the little white-gowned Witch of the North, with two silver-shod feet sticking out from under the house corner.

chapters.title: How Dorothy Saved the Scarecrow
chapters.summary: Dorothy packs bread in a basket, changes into clean gingham, and puts on the Witch of the East's silver shoes to start for the Emerald City. She is feasted and lodged by the rich Munchkin Boq, who warns the journey is long and dangerous. Resting by a cornfield, she frees a talking, brainless Scarecrow from his pole, and he joins her to ask Oz for brains.
chapters.cover_description: Dorothy in her blue-and-white gingham dress and silver shoes lifting a straw-stuffed Scarecrow with painted face and pointed blue Munchkin hat off his tall pole in a ripe cornfield beside the yellow brick road, with Toto barking nearby.

chapters.title: The Road Through the Forest
chapters.summary: Dorothy, Toto, and the Scarecrow continue along the roughening yellow brick road, stopping at noon where Dorothy eats and declares there is no place like home. The Scarecrow tells how he was made days before, exposed by an old crow, and resolved to seek brains from Oz. They press into a dark forest at evening and shelter for the night in a log cottage where Dorothy sleeps while the tireless Scarecrow watches.
chapters.cover_description: Dorothy and Toto walking the rough, broken yellow brick road into a dark forest of huge close trees whose branches meet overhead, guided by the straw-stuffed Scarecrow in his pointed blue hat at dusk.

chapters.title: The Rescue of the Tin Woodman
chapters.summary: Dorothy and the Scarecrow discover a rusted Tin Woodman groaning helpless in the forest and oil his joints to free him. Grateful, he joins their journey to the Emerald City to ask Oz for a heart, telling how the Wicked Witch of the East enchanted his axe so he was gradually made all of tin and lost his heart.
chapters.cover_description: A motionless man made entirely of shining jointed tin standing in a sunlit forest with a sharp axe raised over a half-chopped tree, rusted stiff, while a little girl in gingham oils his neck as a straw scarecrow and small black dog look on.

chapters.title: The Cowardly Lion
chapters.summary: While trekking through a dark forest, Dorothy's party is ambushed by a great Lion who topples the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman and threatens Toto until Dorothy slaps him. The ashamed Lion confesses he is a coward despite being King of Beasts, and begs to join their journey to Oz to ask for courage. Welcomed as a protector, he befriends Toto, and the group continues peacefully until the Tin Woodman rusts his jaws weeping over a crushed beetle and must be oiled.
chapters.cover_description: A small girl in a gingham dress bravely slapping the nose of a huge tawny lion as big as a small horse on a leaf-covered yellow brick road, while a little black dog barks and a stuffed scarecrow and tin man lie toppled nearby in a dark forest.

chapters.title: The Journey to the Great Oz
chapters.summary: The travelers camp overnight in the forest and continue toward the Emerald City, where the Cowardly Lion carries them one by one over a deep rocky ditch. Blocked by a second wider gulf in Kalidah country, they fell a tree for a bridge, defeat two attacking Kalidahs when the Tin Woodman chops it away, then reach a broad river and rest while building a raft to cross to the sunny meadows beyond.
chapters.cover_description: The Cowardly Lion roaring on a fallen tree bridge over a deep rocky gulf as two monstrous bear-bodied, tiger-headed Kalidahs charge across, with Dorothy holding Toto, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman with his axe huddled behind him in a dark gloomy forest.

chapters.title: The Deadly Poppy Field
chapters.summary: After crossing the forest, the travelers build a raft to cross the river but the current sweeps them away, leaving the Scarecrow stranded on his pole until a kind Stork carries him back. Reunited, they walk into a beautiful but deadly meadow of scarlet poppies whose scent puts Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion to sleep, forcing the untiring Scarecrow and Tin Woodman to carry Dorothy to safety while the Lion is left sleeping at the field's edge.
chapters.cover_description: Dorothy fast asleep in a vast brilliant carpet of scarlet poppies with Toto in her arms, carried on a chair made of the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman's hands and arms while the Cowardly Lion sleeps among the flowers nearby beside a river.

chapters.title: The Queen of the Field Mice
chapters.summary: The Tin Woodman saves the Queen of the Field Mice from a great yellow wildcat, earning the loyalty of her thousands of subjects. The Scarecrow devises a plan to have the mice, each bringing string, harnessed to a wooden truck built by the Woodman to pull the Lion from the poisonous poppies. The mice haul the heavy Lion to fresh air, then bid farewell promising future help while the friends wait for him to awaken.
chapters.cover_description: Thousands of tiny gray field mice harnessed with strings to a rough wooden truck hauling a huge sleeping tawny lion out of a vivid bed of red poppies, with a shining tin man and straw scarecrow pushing from behind.

chapters.title: The Guardian of the Gate
chapters.summary: Saved from the poppies by the field mice, the Cowardly Lion rejoins Dorothy, Toto, the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman on the yellow brick road into the green Land of Oz. They shelter at a farmhouse where the farmer warns that the Great Oz never shows himself and can take any form, though he could grant brains, heart, courage and a return to Kansas. Rested and fed, they reach the high green wall of the Emerald City, where the Guardian of the Gates locks green spectacles on them before leading them
chapters.cover_description: Travelers before a towering bright-green wall and a big gate studded with glittering emeralds, bathed in a brilliant green glow, as a little all-green gate guardian fits locked green spectacles onto them.

chapters.title: The Wonderful City of Oz
chapters.summary: Dorothy and her friends enter the green Emerald City and are lodged in the Palace, where Oz agrees to see each alone on successive days. Dorothy as Small and Meek faces Oz as a giant Head, the Scarecrow finds a winged Lady, the Tin Woodman a terrible Beast, and the Lion a Ball of Fire, and each is told their wish requires killing the Wicked Witch of the West. With no other hope, the friends resolve to journey to the Winkies to destroy the Witch despite their fear.
chapters.cover_description: Dorothy the Small and Meek standing alone in the round emerald Throne Room before the enormous bodiless giant Head on the green marble throne, emeralds glittering under a sun-bright ceiling light.

chapters.title: The Search for the Wicked Witch
chapters.summary: Dorothy and her friends journey west to destroy the Wicked Witch of the West, surviving attacks by wolves, crows, bees, and Winkies through the sacrifices of the Woodman, Scarecrow, and Lion. The Witch uses her last command of the Golden Cap to have the Winged Monkeys destroy the Woodman and Scarecrow and capture the Lion and Dorothy. Enslaved in the castle, Dorothy accidentally melts the Witch with a bucket of water when the Witch steals one of her Silver Shoes, freeing herself and the Lion.
chapters.cover_description: A small girl in a white dress hurls a bucket of water over a shrieking Wicked Witch in the castle kitchen as the Witch melts into a brown shapeless mass on the floorboards, one stolen silver shoe on her skinny foot.

chapters.title: The Rescue
chapters.summary: After melting the Wicked Witch, Dorothy frees the Lion and the Winkies, who joyfully help rescue the battered Tin Woodman and the scattered Scarecrow. The Winkie tinsmiths mend the Tin Woodman with patches and a new gold-handled axe, and the friends are tearfully reunited. After happy days and farewell gifts, they don the Golden Cap and set out again for the Emerald City to claim Oz's promises.
chapters.cover_description: Dorothy in her gingham dress and Toto standing with the Cowardly Lion, Tin Woodman and Scarecrow reunited in the sunny yellow courtyard of the Wicked Witch's Yellow Castle as joyful Winkies feast and dance around them.

chapters.title: The Winged Monkeys
chapters.summary: Lost in the fields after destroying the Wicked Witch of the West, Dorothy and her friends wander for days until the Queen of the Field Mice tells Dorothy to use the charm inside the Golden Cap. Dorothy summons the Winged Monkeys, who carry the party toward the Emerald City while the Monkey King tells how Gayelette bound his people to obey the Cap's owner thrice. The Monkeys set the travelers safely down at the Emerald City gates, having used one of Dorothy's three wishes.
chapters.cover_description: Dorothy riding high in the sky in a chair made of the hands of two giant winged monkeys, with the band of winged monkeys carrying the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Lion and Toto through the air above gardens and woods toward the green shining walls of the Emerald City.

chapters.title: The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible
chapters.summary: After melting the Wicked Witch of the West, Dorothy and her friends return to the Emerald City to claim Oz's promises, but Oz avoids them until threatened with the Winged Monkeys. In the Throne Room Toto topples a screen, exposing Oz as a common ventriloquist balloonist from Omaha who fooled everyone with paper, costume, and cotton-fire tricks. He agrees to grant brains, heart, courage and a way home to Kansas tomorrow if they keep his humbug secret.
chapters.cover_description: The Cowardly Lion's mighty roar topples a corner screen in the empty Throne Room, revealing a frightened little bald old man hiding behind it as Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman and Toto stare in shock.

chapters.title: The Magic Art of the Great Humbug
chapters.summary: Oz grants the Scarecrow bran-new brains mixed with pins and needles, the Tin Woodman a silk sawdust-stuffed heart, and the Cowardly Lion a drink of supposed courage, leaving all three delighted. Alone afterward, Oz reflects that his humbug easily satisfied their imagination, but he has no idea how to actually carry Dorothy back to Kansas.
chapters.cover_description: The little bald Wizard stuffing the Scarecrow's cloth head with bran mixed with pins and needles in the jeweled Throne Room, the Scarecrow's head bulging at the top with his new brains.

chapters.title: How the Balloon Was Launched
chapters.summary: After three sad days of waiting, Oz summons Dorothy and reveals his plan to escape across the desert in a homemade hot-air balloon made of green silk. Dorothy helps him sew the balloon and build the basket, and Oz announces the Scarecrow will rule in his absence. When the inflated balloon breaks its ropes just as Dorothy is delayed finding Toto, Oz rises away alone forever, leaving Dorothy stranded and the people grieving his loss.
chapters.cover_description: A giant green silk hot-air balloon tugging at its ropes over a wood fire in front of the Emerald City Palace, with the Wizard waving goodbye from the wicker basket as Dorothy runs toward him carrying little Toto while a crowd watches.

chapters.title: Away to the South
chapters.summary: After Oz departs in the balloon, Dorothy mourns losing her way home while the Tin Woodman weeps for Oz and the Scarecrow becomes ruler of the Emerald City. When the Winged Monkeys refuse to carry Dorothy over the desert because they cannot leave Oz country, the soldier with green whiskers advises seeking Glinda, the Good Witch of the South. Dorothy and her three friends all vow to journey south together to ask Glinda for help getting Dorothy back to Kansas.
chapters.cover_description: The straw-stuffed Scarecrow sitting proudly on the grand green emerald throne in the Throne Room, with Dorothy in her gingham dress holding the Golden Cap while a flock of Winged Monkeys bursts through the tall open window.

chapters.title: Attacked by the Fighting Trees
chapters.summary: After a fond farewell at the Emerald City gates where they return their green spectacles, Dorothy and her friends set out south for Glinda's land in high spirits and camp under the stars. The next morning they are stopped by a row of Fighting Trees that seize and hurl back the Scarecrow until the Tin Woodman chops their way through, freeing Toto. Passing easily through the rest of the wood, they are then blocked by a high, smooth white china wall which the Tin Woodman proposes to climb with a la
chapters.cover_description: The Tin Woodman swinging his sharp axe to chop a living branch of a giant Fighting Tree as it seizes the straw-stuffed Scarecrow in mid-air, with Dorothy, the Lion and little Toto watching at the dark edge of the thick forest.

chapters.title: The Dainty China Country
chapters.summary: The travelers climb over a high wall into the fragile Dainty China Country, where everything and everyone is made of painted china. After accidentally breaking a milkmaid's cow's leg, Dorothy learns from a beautiful Princess and a cracked clown that china folk are happier in their own land. The party crosses carefully and escapes over the far wall, breaking only a church with the Lion's tail.
chapters.cover_description: Four travelers and a small dog perched atop a high china wall looking down on a shining white miniature country of tiny painted china houses, barns, fences, and knee-high china people and animals.

chapters.title: The Lion Becomes the King of Beasts
chapters.summary: Traveling through bogs into a vast old forest, Dorothy's party discovers hundreds of beasts terrorized by a giant man-eating spider. The Lion agrees to kill the monster in exchange for being made King of the Forest, then springs on the sleeping spider and severs its slender neck with one clawed blow. The grateful beasts bow to him as their King, and he promises to return to rule them after Dorothy is safely on her way to Kansas.
chapters.cover_description: A great tawny lion with a shaggy mane leaping onto the back of a huge black hairy spider-monster with tree-trunk legs in a vast ancient oak forest, striking its slender neck with a clawed paw while hundreds of forest beasts watch from a clearing.

chapters.title: The Country of the Quadlings
chapters.summary: Blocked from crossing a steep hill to the Quadlings by the armless Hammer-Heads whose shooting heads knock down the Scarecrow and Lion, the travelers are carried safely over by the Winged Monkeys when Dorothy uses the Golden Cap. Set down in the rich red Quadling country, they enjoy dinner at a farmhouse and then walk south to Glinda's beautiful Castle, where they are admitted at once.
chapters.cover_description: The Winged Monkeys soaring high over a steep rocky hill carrying Dorothy, Toto, the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman and Lion, while armless Hammer-Heads below shoot their flat-topped heads into the air in vexation.

chapters.title: Glinda The Good Witch Grants Dorothy’s Wish
chapters.summary: Dorothy and her friends are received by the beautiful Good Witch Glinda in her ruby throne room. Glinda takes the Golden Cap in exchange for showing Dorothy home, promising to use its three commands to return the Scarecrow to the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman to the Winkies, and the Lion to his forest before freeing the Winged Monkeys. Glinda then reveals the Silver Shoes can carry Dorothy home in three steps, and after tearful farewells Dorothy clicks her heels and wakes on the Kansas prairie,
chapters.cover_description: Dorothy with Toto in her arms clicking the heels of her sparkling Silver Shoes together three times before Glinda's ruby throne, as the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman and Cowardly Lion watch tearfully.

chapters.title: Home Again
chapters.summary: Dorothy runs to Aunt Em outside the Kansas farmhouse and is folded into her arms and kissed. When asked where she came from, Dorothy gravely says she has returned from the Land of Oz with Toto. She exclaims how glad she is to be at home again.
chapters.cover_description: Aunt Em kneeling in a dusty Kansas farmyard embracing a little girl in a gingham dress and sunbonnet as she runs toward her, with a small black dog at her side and a farmhouse and cabbage patch behind them in bright daylight.
